A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SafeDialBench. Their text, figures, tables and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization and expansion in v4.

before.justification: v3 reports original evaluations of 17 LLMs, human agreement measurements, attack comparisons and per-turn analyses, including Tables 2–4 and appendix Tables 9–11.

after.justification: v4 retains original empirical results and expands evaluation to 19 LLMs, adding dataset-diversity measurements, statistical analyses, evaluator validation, and attack/defense comparisons.

M1.justification: The specified second-tier taxonomy removes Discrimination under Morality and Violence under Ethics as separate safety points (v3 Figure 2/Table 6 versus v4 Figure 2(a)/Table 4). The seven attack strategies, three-ability scoring prompts, golden-context procedure and minimum-score aggregation remain unchanged. Expanded generation descriptions primarily disclose existing procedures.

E1.justification: Both retain 4,053 Chinese and English dialogues across 22 scenarios, six safety domains and 3–10 turns, with identical language/domain counts (v3 Table 7; v4 Table 6). Added studies sample this corpus or change comparison methods and evaluation procedures. The taxonomy edits do not establish removal of represented data or tasks.

E2.justification: QwQ-32B and DeepSeek-R1 join the retained model comparisons in Table 2 and the corresponding appendix tables. More substantially, v4 newly evaluates Actorattack and Crescendo against the seven attack strategies (Table 14), and X-Boundary and NBF-LLM against vanilla models (Table 15). v3 contains neither external attack nor defense comparison.

E3.justification: v4 introduces ASR with a below-seven score threshold, balanced 300-dialogue statistical and prompt-robustness evaluations, and a 50-dialogue defense evaluation. The per-turn study changes from four dimensions using three attack methods to six dimensions under fallacy attack, replacing the fairness/role-play and morality/reference-attack settings. Golden contexts and temperature zero remain the main evaluation settings.

E4.justification: v4 adds a controlled comparison of dialogue-source diversity (D.3), evaluator false-positive analysis (F.3), a DeepSeek-R1 reasoning case (G.4), defense-effectiveness analysis (G.8), and sensitivity to scoring-prompt modifications (G.10). The per-turn analysis is also revised and expanded. Earlier attack radars and existing case studies are retained.

E5.justification: v3 reports agreement percentages without repeated-test uncertainty. v4 adds a three-test analysis on 300 dialogues with mean-plus-standard-deviation reporting in Tables 10–13, and variation across three evaluation prompts in Tables 16–17. F.3 newly specifies Fleiss’ Kappa and modal expert consensus. This does not establish repeated full-corpus evaluation; the prose also inconsistently calls standard deviations confidence intervals.

E6.justification: All matched existing numerical cells in Table 2 and the judge/language appendix tables are unchanged. v4 adds two model rows and extensive ASR, diversity, validation, attack/defense and robustness results. For example, the new 50-dialogue defense comparison reports Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct ASR of 54% vanilla versus 32% with X-Boundary (Table 15). Some per-turn results are replaced under changed attack settings, and v3’s aggregate Table 3 is omitted.

T1.justification: Neither version develops formal mathematical theory, assumptions, theorems or proofs. Despite its title, v4 G.11, Theoretical Discovery for Jailbreak Attack and Defense, presents qualitative mechanisms and hypotheses rather than formal derivations or established mathematical properties.

C1.justification: The central benchmark and three-ability evaluation contributions remain. The abstract changes its emphasized safety leaders from Yi-34B-Chat and GLM4-9B-Chat to Yi-34B-Chat, MoonShot-v1 and ChatGPT-4o. The introduction and conclusion add Baichuan2-7B-Chat’s ASR vulnerability and ChatGPT-4o’s lowest-ASR finding.

C2.justification: v4 adds substantive explanations of morality/ethics boundaries, generation bias, cross-language generalization and reasoning-model vulnerability as alignment failure. G.9–G.12 introduce mitigation recommendations, context-poisoning and safety-memory hypotheses, and broader defense implications. These considerably extend v3’s interpretations; the mitigation recommendations are prospective, and the original Limitations paragraph remains.

D1.justification: v4 substantially expands construction documentation: annotator interaction and stopping rules, approximately 15 daily annotators, complete peer cross-checking, 20%–50% expert audits, and a 95% batch acceptance threshold. It also adds model-access information, a project-page pointer and a statement that datasets and core code are supplied. These are chiefly new disclosures, not evidence that the retained dataset was reconstructed.

R1.justification: Section 2 and Appendix A substantially expand positioning around recent work, including LinguaSafe, X-Teaming, CoA, ASJA and StegoAttack. Additional discussion connects the benchmark to reasoning attacks and defenses, including H-CoT, Mousetrap and X-Boundary. v4 also explicitly claims priority for combining bilingual, multi-turn, diverse-attack and fine-grained evaluation.

P1.justification: The detailed taxonomy subsections are condensed in the main text and rewritten within Appendix B. The introduction and generation/evaluation explanations are extensively expanded, while Appendices D, F and G receive substantial subdivision and narrative restructuring. Title, author ordering, affiliations and back matter also change.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column formatting to a single-column ICLR layout. Figure 2 combines a revised taxonomy with a new generation workflow; Figure 4 adds ASR and redisplays unchanged human agreement values. Per-turn plots expand from four to six panels, model-size plots are rearranged, numerous tables and illustrations are added, and v3’s aggregate Table 3 is removed.

improvement.justification: The added external comparisons, evaluator and prompt-robustness checks, and explicit annotation audits improve the benchmark’s support and transparency beyond v3. The gain is limited by new reporting problems: G.7 overstates Topic Change’s superiority over Actorattack and Crescendo relative to Table 14, and G.1 describes reported standard deviations as confidence intervals. These issues weaken the reliability of some expanded interpretations.
